metadata.target_audience: Parents of school-aged children and teenagers (Ages 6–17)
metadata.core_objective: Prevent conflict escalation during boundary enforcement using co-regulation techniques.

topics.title: The Neuroscience of Escalation: Flipping the Lid
topics.summary: Understanding nervous system responses during boundary enforcement.

key_concepts.description: Controls fight, flight, freeze, or fawn responses. Logic shuts down when triggered.
Controls reasoning, impulse control, empathy, and problem-solving.
Dysregulated parents cannot regulate a dysregulated child. Children mirror parental nervous systems.

steps.name: Regulate
steps.action: Somatic and physical calm. Lower tone, slow speech, relax posture.

steps.name: Relate
steps.action: Emotional connection and validation of feelings before addressing the infraction.

steps.name: Reason
steps.action: Logical consequences and problem-solving after nervous system equilibrium is restored.

activities.title: Identifying Personal Escalation Triggers
activities.instructions: Map physical warning signs and environmental triggers to construct calming strategies.

activities.title: Scripting the Regulate-Relate-Reason Response
activities.instructions: Apply the 3-step sequence to common high-stress confrontations.

tasks.title: Parent Time-Out Protocol
tasks.action: Establish an explicit phrase to pause conversations during personal emotional escalation.

tasks.title: Post-Escalation Repair Routine
tasks.action: Execute a 3-part repair process (Acknowledge, Take Ownership, Re-anchor Boundary) if emotional composure breaks.

quiz.question: According to neuroscience-informed parenting, what must happen before a child can process a logical consequence?
options: A) They must feel remorse and apologize.
B) Their nervous system must return to a regulated state.
C) They must spend time isolated in their bedroom.
D) The parent must explain the rule at least three times.

quiz.question: Which order represents the correct sequence for effective de-escalation?
